scope: nine modes in one SBF: five marked q18 layer-zero hash/recombination controls; the three existing Component-B dense/rejected controls; and one compact degree-27 candidate measuring nineteen-lane fourth-claim aggregation, compact state setup, and four dual folds; no full proof parser or integrated v5 verifier
authority_note: This nine-mode build adds the compact candidate while retaining the dense and rejected controls. Adding a mode changes compiled control flow and code layout, so only comparisons recorded together in this artifact are authoritative.
measurement_method: Layer-zero modes retain their two marked intervals. Relation modes use three matched intervals: common relation setup plus canonical lane-claim parsing/gamma aggregation; terminal-weight setup; then the existing four relation folds and final dot (or the explicitly rejected standalone 1023-term dot). The compact mode starts ten repeated-squaring ladders plus one singleton, derives the remaining powers as the folds consume them, and carries an exact degree-27 truncation through four folds without a 1024-value vector. Every mode is submitted three times. Relation modes use a fixed 16-byte post-marker sink; sink hashing and remaining transaction overhead are outside the final marker, and transaction totals are recorded separately.

comparison_caveat: The clean forecast signals use matched three-comparison mode-selection paths: generic26_fused to generic16_fused for width, and generic16_nonfused to generic16_fused for fusion. The raw generic non-fused width and width-26 fusion deltas each contain an observed 38-CU mode-selection asymmetry. Production26 already uses the current fused three-product helper, so its delta to generic16_fused is not an old-v4-to-v5 comparison.
component_b_default_heap_observation: The retained literal fixed-array control exceeded the 4 KiB SBF stack and was moved to an algebraically identical heap vector. With the ordinary 2.3 KiB layer-zero sink allocated after its Dense folds, the default SBF heap then exhausted; relation modes therefore use a fixed 16-byte post-marker sink. The compact candidate itself requests no dynamic heap and its 540-byte fixed state builds below the SBF stack limit, but an integrated verifier still needs a lifetime audit with the production parser and sink.
component_b_binding_caveat: Both the retained Dense control and the compact candidate batch four functionals as [1, kappa, kappa^2, kappa^3]. The compact path carries the exact public degree-27 row covector through the existing gamma-combined relation and authenticates it only through the existing pre-challenge circle-FRI commitment/pass. This raises the functional-batching Schwartz-Zippel degree from two to three and requires a soundness-ledger update. The probe measures verifier arithmetic and exact dual-fold correspondence; it does not by itself prove transcript binding, hiding, or Rust-to-Lean correspondence. A plain standalone row dot is not a binding commitment and is reported only as a rejected cost control.

conclusion: The compact degree-27 candidate adds 9555 CU for nineteen fourth claims, 3364 CU for compact state setup, and 62979 CU for four exact dual folds/final dot: 75898 marked CU in total, with a separately recorded 75900-CU transaction delta. Against the provisional 112000-CU envelope this isolated seam leaves 36102 CU, so it fits that arithmetic envelope by itself; this is not a full-v5 fit claim. Its fixed state is 540 bytes and requests no dynamic heap, avoiding a 16384-byte dense payload. The retained dense control adds 748744 marked CU; the retained rejected standalone construction adds 709497 marked CU. Functional batching still uses [1, kappa, kappa^2, kappa^3] and needs the soundness-ledger update. Layer-zero controls remain: matched fused width saves 37631 CU and width-16 fusion saves 21784 CU.
